apia-4.name: Palolo Deep Marine Reserve
apia-4.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach way 188691920 'Palolo Deep' (nominatim), agrees within ~40 m with Wikivoyage Apia listing geo (-13.8252,-171.7575); confidence HIGH. Moved ~40 m from placement point. Note pins.1 recommended the reef centroid (natural=reef, 416 m offshore) which was not used.

cost.note: Wikivoyage price=WST5; airial.travel agrees ($5 Tala). Not from an operator page (samoa.travel blocked). No park pass applies (nt.gov.au list is irrelevant).

apia-4.ticketUrl_note: Likely official page on samoa.travel (Samoa Tourism Authority), returns 403 to scripts for https://www.samoa.travel/ ; orchestrator to check in a real browser. No guessed URL recorded.

facts.fact: Official underwater park / marine reserve at Vaiala Beach, the only beach in Apia east of the harbour; mostly coral gravel
Snorkelling improves further out (about a quarter mile swim), with occasional turtles and blacktip reef sharks
Check the tide chart at the gate: at low tide it is a long paddle over sharp coral; best on the incoming tide
Snorkels can be rented on site; entry WST 5

apia-4.bio: Vaiala Beach marine reserve east of Apia where a swim past the reef edge finds turtles and blacktip reef sharks, best on a rising tide.

togitogiga-falls.name: Togitogiga Falls
togitogiga-falls.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall node 5593724712 'Togitogiga Waterfalls' (nominatim); MEDIUM (single precise OSM feature of right type). Moved ~0 m from placement point. pins.1 recommended place=village Togitogiga (1.4 km away), rejected as a town point.

cost.note: ArrivalGuides: 'no entry fee here'. Other (non-official) sources mention a small village fee of a few tala or 5 tala; unresolved, treated as free. Not covered by any park pass found (Samoa has none in parkPasses.ts). Parking/bus fares not counted.

togitogiga-falls.ticketUrl_note: Managing body is Samoa's Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment; Samoa Tourism Authority page on samoa.travel is 403 to scripts. Orchestrator to check samoa.travel in a real browser for a Togitogiga or O Le Pupu-Pu'e page; none recorded meanwhile.

facts.fact: A series of gentle waterfalls separated by cool waterholes for swimming; best in the wet season
Reached by the access road for O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park; parking area, changing rooms and toilets on site
Within O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park on Upolu's south coast, in Salailua village

togitogiga-falls.bio: Cascades and cool swimming holes inside O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park, with changing rooms, best in the wet season.

lalomanu-beach.name: Lalomanu Beach
lalomanu-beach.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach 'Lalomanu Beach' (nominatim); MEDIUM; ~0 m from placement point; Wikivoyage Lalomanu listing geo (-14.045971,-171.445341) is ~380 m east, not used.

cost.note: Beach with beach-fale accommodation; no entry charge found in any source; beach fale stays are separate. Unverified that no village fee applies.

lalomanu-beach.ticketUrl_note: Beach with many independent fale operators and no single steward.

facts.fact: Area in the south-east with beautiful beaches and views of small idyllic islands
Lalomanu is a village on Upolu's east coast, in Atua district, population 712
Namua Island boat leaves from the mainland a few minutes' drive from Lalomanu Beach; turtles often seen on the short boat trip
The 2009 tsunami damaged the lagoon reef but plenty of fish remain; beach fales and a dive shop operate on the beach

lalomanu-beach.bio: A white-sand beach on Upolu's south-east coast looking out to the small Aleipata islands, with beach fales and boats to Namua Island.

savaii-2.name: Saleaula Lava Field
savaii-2.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=attraction node 3329465788 "Virgin's grave", the guided visitor stop in the lava field; corroborated by Wikivoyage Savaii listing geo (-13.45009,-172.3335) ~150 m away; MEDIUM. Moved ~140 m from placement point. Not used: OSM tourism=attraction 'Sale'aula Lava Fields' node at -13.4591031,-172.3176139 (1.8 km SE) and place=town node (village point).

cost.note: Wikivoyage: 'A fee is charged', no amount. WST 5 per adult is from a 2022 budget-travel article snippet (eglobaltravelmedia.com.au, not loaded in full) and unverified; locals collect it. One other source says no formal fee. Treat as approximate.

savaii-2.ticketUrl_note: Run by the village (Saleaula Women's Committee per a travel site); no own site. Samoa Tourism Authority listing on samoa.travel is 403 to scripts, orchestrator to check. None recorded meanwhile.

facts.fact: Lava from Mt Matavanu eruptions destroyed Sale'aula and Salago villages, flowing over 40 square miles to the sea
Eruptions ran 1905 to 1911; lava is up to 400 ft deep
More accessible than the Mt Matavanu fields, 30-minute drive east of the ferry
A guide is needed to see the two churches that escaped complete destruction and the Virgin's Grave; a fee is charged

savaii-2.bio: Lava field from the 1905-11 Mt Matavanu eruptions that buried two villages, with guided visits to the surviving churches and the Virgin's Grave.

savaii-7.coordinates_source: OSM natural=peak node 'Mauga Tafua' (the volcanic crater the walk climbs), MEDIUM; ~3.9 km from the Wikivoyage listing geo (-13.7833,-172.2167) which is a vague area point. No OSM route found for the walk, so the pin is the crater, not a route midpoint; check against the village-run trail map if one exists.

cost.note: UNVERIFIED: Wikivoyage price blank and no source found for any fee or access charge. Cost not set; orchestrator to decide (hold, or free/open if a visitor source confirms).

savaii-7.ticketUrl_note: No official site found; samoa.travel BLOCKED (403) for any listing.

facts.fact: Good stands of rainforest and excellent birdwatching on the south-east peninsula
A walk leads up to the volcanic crater that dominates Tafua
OSM marks the crater peak as Mauga Tafua

savaii-7.bio: Rainforest preserve on Savai'i's south-east peninsula, good for birdwatching, with a walk up to the volcanic crater of Mauga Tafua.
